rationale: Real BingX BTC-USDT/1d retention as of 2026-07-28 is 1,901 daily bars, zero internal gaps, earliest 2021-05-14T00:00:00Z, latest 2026-07-27T00:00:00Z -- confirmed by a real backfill.py run against the live production endpoint (not a binary-search probe), see .planning/sr-t-daily-data-path.md. UNLIKE configs/research/holdout.json (15m) and configs/research/holdout_1h.json (1h), this config sets holdout_side='before': the holdout is the EARLIEST slice (everything before the cutoff) and research data is everything at/after it. Reasoning, which is about what has been DONE to the data rather than where it sits on the calendar: CLAUDE.md's Strategy Research Methodology defines a holdout as a split that 'must exist and stay untouched... Touching it converts it from a validation check into just more training data.' Every one of the 1,839 backtest_run records in runs/experiments.jsonl has data_range.start_ms >= 1714212000000 (2024-04-27T10:00:00Z) -- verified directly against the real log, across all 22 distinct start values -- because that timestamp is the floor of BingX's 1h retention, where primary strategy research has lived since Strategy Research Task F. Eight strategy families' worth of parameter search, diagnosis and eligibility judgment have therefore been shaped by data from 2024-04-27 onward and by NOTHING before it. A trailing 1d holdout would reserve data this project has already studied intensively through a shorter timeframe's lens; the early window is the only genuinely untouched data this project has. Choosing the calendar-late window here would satisfy convention and defeat the purpose. CUTOFF CHOICE: 1714176000000 is 2024-04-27T00:00:00Z, i.e. the earliest-ever-touched instant (2024-04-27T10:00:00Z) floored -- not rounded up -- to the 86,400,000ms daily grid. Flooring puts the one partially-overlapping daily bar (2024-04-27, which spans 10 hours that logged runs have seen) on the RESEARCH side, so no bar in the holdout covers any wall-clock minute any logged run has ever observed; rounding up would have pulled that half-seen bar into the holdout. Holdout: 1,079 daily bars, 2021-05-14 through 2024-04-26 inclusive (~2.95 years). Research: 822 daily bars, 2024-04-27 through 2026-07-27 (~2.25 years). SIZING, stated plainly: this holdout is LARGER than the research split, deliberately breaking the '15-25% of available data' framing the other two configs follow. That framing assumes a dataset whose non-holdout remainder is itself untouched, so the split is a free design choice about proportion. Here it is not a choice at all -- the boundary is a historical fact about where contamination begins, and moving it in either direction either wastes virgin data or admits touched data into the holdout. What the size buys is detection power: at ~2.95 years the smallest annualized Sharpe distinguishable from zero at one-sided 95% (detectable Sharpe ~= 1.645/sqrt(years)) is ~0.96, versus ~2.57 for the 1h config's 150-day trailing holdout -- this window can actually confirm or reject a realistic edge, where the trailing one mostly cannot. DISCLOSED COSTS: (a) 822 daily bars is thin for walk-forward at this granularity; the fold sizing for 1d research is deliberately NOT decided here and belongs to whichever task first runs a strategy on this data. (b) The 1d research window covers the same calendar span that configs/research/holdout_1h.json reserves as the 1h holdout (2026-02-26T08:00:00Z onward); those are different series and different configs, but a future task intending to run BOTH the 1h and 1d holdout confirmations should be aware of the overlap rather than discover it afterwards. (c) BingX retention is rolling, not a fixed archive: the earliest 1d bar drifts forward over time, so this holdout SHRINKS on every future backfill while the research side grows. The cutoff is fixed and must not be moved to chase it. WRITTEN BEFORE ANY RESULT: this cutoff and rationale were committed before any strategy was written, run or evaluated against 1d data -- the 1d interval was only wired into data/_grid.py in the same task that wrote this file, and no backtest of any kind has ever been run on it. That ordering is the whole point; a cutoff chosen after seeing a result on the data it splits is not a holdout.
